title: Study manifest
description: The shape of a study manifest. The contract version is the last segment of this $id. Paths in a manifest are relative to the manifest's own directory.

contract_version.description: The contract version the manifest was written for; must equal the last segment of this schema's $id.

research_questions.description: Ids of the research questions the batteries attached to this study answer.

statistical_questions.description: Ids of the computable statistical questions derived from the research questions.

protocol_version.description: Version of the protocol the data were produced under.

evolution_log.description: Every change to the plan or protocol after it was first fixed, with the reason. Empty while nothing has changed.

id.description: Unique within the manifest; `compare` pairs datasets of two manifests by this id.

path.description: Data file, relative to the manifest.

dictionary.description: The data dictionary inline, or the path (relative to the manifest) of a JSON file holding it.

unit.description: Name of the dictionary variable whose levels are independent observations (a subject, a plate, a site). It may repeat across rows; the `id` variables, jointly, are what key the rows.

name.description: Column header, exactly as in the file.

units.description: Required for integer and number variables, checked by the script; the word unitless when there are none.

allowed_values.description: The only values the column may hold (outside missing codes).

range.description: [min, max], inclusive; for integer and number variables.

missing_codes.description: Cell contents that mean 'no value' for this variable; any other missing-looking cell is a problem.

code_commit.description: Commit of the code that produced or processed the data.

seeds.description: Random seeds; required, and non-empty, when the origin is simulated-null or simulated-effect (checked by the script).

instrument.description: What produced the data: a device, a survey, a simulator and its version.

dates.description: When the data were collected or generated, as YYYY-MM-DD.

stage.description: Where the study stood: before any data, after a pilot or a simulation, after the data of this study were seen.

change.description: The old and the new content, concretely.

reason.description: What was learned that motivated it.

agreed_by.description: Who agreed: the user, the parent agent, the agent that supplied the number.

effect_on_claim.description: Which results remain confirmatory and which become exploratory.
